# SpotVault

> Free app that keeps your music offline. The Windows app saves playlists from Spotify, YouTube, YouTube Music and SoundCloud as audio files with cover art, one folder per playlist, and can search for any single song and save it into a playlist. The Android and iPhone app copies those playlists from the PC over Wi-Fi, plays them with no signal, and can add new songs by search (the PC downloads them and sends them back).

- Website: https://spotvault-web.vercel.app/
- Source code: https://github.com/sarathlal-12/spotvault
- Downloads (v1.3.0): https://github.com/sarathlal-12/spotvault/releases/tag/v1.3.0
- Price: free. No account needed; everything runs locally.
- Platforms: Windows (installer), Android (APK), iPhone (IPA, sideloaded with AltStore)
- Author: Sarath Lal (https://github.com/sarathlal-12)

## How it works

1. Paste a public playlist link (Spotify, YouTube, YouTube Music or SoundCloud) into SpotVault on Windows. It saves every song with cover art into its own folder. Later syncs only fetch new songs.
2. Use Search songs to find any single track, and save it into one of your playlists.
3. Click Connect phone on the PC. The phone app connects over the same Wi-Fi using the PC's address and a 6-digit PIN, and copies every playlist across. Interrupted copies resume.
4. On the phone, Search > Find new songs lets you listen to a song and save it to a playlist; the PC downloads it and sends it back over Wi-Fi.
5. Play offline on the phone: playlists, Liked Songs, search, shuffle, repeat, queue editing, sleep timer, playback speed and lock-screen controls.

## Notes

- Playlists must be public or shared by link; private playlists can't be read.
- Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi, and Windows Firewall must allow SpotVault on Private networks.
- The Windows app has everything built in (including the audio converter); nothing else to install.
- Not on the Google Play Store or Apple App Store; it is distributed through GitHub releases.
